micronarrative: I grew up in a small Michigan town where I’ve seen protests for human rights and immigration support unfold peacefully, with people handing out tea instead of shouting. In the scenario, the contrast between hostile demands for border enforcement and calm advocacy feels familiar—like the difference between my first job in hotel housekeeping, where yelling only drowned out what mattered, and the protests I’ve witnessed, where respect let ideas be heard. As a working-class person, I recognize the fear of being at the bottom of society’s ladder, where your family’s dignity can feel under attack. I try to speak without shifting my tone, believing others deserve to be heard even when we disagree. The everyday residents in the scenario who stay neutral? I get that too—sometimes survival means keeping your head down while chaos swirls around you.
